title: Signal taxonomy and dashboards + trace sampling notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick internal working doc to capture a signal taxonomy (metrics + traces), concrete dashboard wireframes, and a pragmatic trace-sampling strategy for model inference services. Not final — want feedback from SRE, serving-runtime, and product console teams.

Audience:
- Observability SMEs
- Serving runtime owners
- Platform engineers building dashboard templates

Context / why this now:
- Dedicated rollout + Private installs require tighter SLO visibility across model variants.
- Current dashboards show raw latency but lack batch-aware signals and trace sampling is too low-cost (we miss slow tail).
- Need consistent metric names and a minimal trace enrichment schema for root-cause.

High-level goals:
- One canonical metric namespace that all services use (names + units).
- Dashboards that surface SLOs, slow-tail drivers, and batching/backpressure indicators.
- Trace sampling strategy: low-cost baseline + targeted high-fidelity for anomalies and error bursts.

Metric definitions (proposal — short-form, normalize to prometheus/datadog style):
1) request.count — total API requests received (unit: count). tag: route, customer_tier, region, model_name.
2) request.tokens.in — input tokens per request (unit: tokens). aggregate: p50,p95,p99.
3) request.tokens.out — output tokens emitted. p50,p95.
4) invoke.latency.ms — wall-clock from request-arrival to first-byte sent (unit: ms). quantiles: p50/p90/p95/p99. tags: model_version, deployment_zone, batch_id (if batched).
5) generate.latency.per_token.ms — per-tokening time (ms/token) to detect slow kernel paths.
6) kvcache.hit_rate — fraction of KV cache hits (unit: percent). important to explain cache priming impact on latency.
7) batch.size — distribution of batch sizes being executed. (histogram)
8) queue.depth — number of requests waiting to be batched/executed.
9) gpu.utilization.percent — GPU (%) per node. track by node-type and machine-id.
10) oom.count — OOM events (count) with tags: model_name, quantization_profile.
11) fallback.count — automatic fallback to smaller/cheaper model variant (count).
12) model.quality.regression.alerts — count of eval failures tied to promptset checks (integration with Optimize).

Notes on naming: keep dots for hierarchy (easier in dashboards), always include units in metric metadata, and require these tags: request_id, model_name, model_version, route, customer_tier, region, deployment_zone.

Trace enrichment fields (span attributes we must record):
- request_id (UUID)
- route (API route name)
- model_name, model_version
- batch_id (nullable)
- tokens_in, tokens_out
- client_tier (free/paid/dedicated)
- gpu_node, container_id
- kvcache_hit (bool) or kvcache_hit_ratio (float)
- sampling_reason (auto / error / latency / manual)

Trace sampling strategy (practical + low-cost):
1) Baseline sampling: 0.5% of all requests (uniform random). Tag traces with sampling_reason=baseline.
2) Priority sampling rules (override baseline and sample at 100%):
   - error.status != OK (any 5xx or internal failures) -> always sample (sampling_reason=error).
   - invoke.latency > p99_threshold_for_route -> sample N (default 100%) for that route for 10 minutes (sampling_reason=slow_tail).
   - fallback.count spike detection: if fallback rate > baseline_threshold over sliding 1m -> sample 100% of requests for affected customer/route.
   - KV cache warmup anomalies: if kvcache.hit_rate drops > 30% relative to 1h baseline -> sample.
3) Adaptive tail-sampling: maintain a small reservoir of high-latency requests per minute (e.g., top 50 slowest) to always capture tail patterns.
4) Manual trace capture: console button to force sample for a request_id (for support replication).

Retention and cost controls:
- Keep full traces (spans + logs) for 7 days in hot storage.
- Long-term aggregated trace metadata (span counts, top-error signatures) for 90 days.
- For private deployments, provide a knob to reduce baseline sample to 0.1% or increase to 1% depending on contract.

Dashboard wireframes / layout (priority order) — each row = 3–4 panels:
Row A (SLO + traffic overview):
- SLO status panel (error budget burn, p95 latency vs SLO)
- Traffic: requests/min, avg tokens/request, active connections
- Capacity: GPU utilization aggregated by pool

Row B (latency and batching):
- p50/90/95/99 latency timeseries, stacked by model_version
- Latency heatmap by route x hour-of-day (detect scheduling vs load issues)
- Batch size distribution histogram + mean batch latency correlation scatterplot (batch size vs latency)

Row C (traces + errors):
- Error rate timeseries with drilldown links to traces (filter by sampling_reason)
- Top trace root causes (tagged by model_version, kvcache_hit=false, OOM) — derived from sampled traces
- Trace waterfall example panel (link to open trace in tracing UI)

Row D (infrastructure + queueing):
- Queue depth per shard/pool (alerts if > threshold)
- Pod/container memory and GPU memory pressure
- OOM count + recent OOM trace links

Panel implementation notes (quick):
- Always include a quick filter bar: model_name, model_version, region, customer_tier, route, time range.
- When possible, panels should link directly to traces or logs (request_id param).
- Use derived metrics to avoid expensive raw queries (e.g., aggregated p95 computed in ingestion).

Alerting suggestions (starter thresholds — tune per route):
- p95 latency breach > SLO by 15% for 3 consecutive minutes -> page oncall.
- error.rate > 0.5% of traffic for 1m -> page (or 5xx spike).
- kvcache.hit_rate drop > 25% relative to 1h baseline -> notify infra team (possible model rollout issue).
- queue.depth > 2x steady-state for 60s -> SRE investigate backlog/batching regression.

Open questions / discussion items (need decisions):
- Baseline sample rate: 0.5% vs 0.1% for hosted by default? (trade-off: tail coverage vs cost)
- Should we store per-token latency histograms or only per-request? (memory/cost tradeoff)
- How to instrument async or streaming responses: what defines 'latency' for streaming? first-byte vs full completion?
- Standardize quantization_profile label values across runtime (we currently have inconsistent names).

Action items (owners):
- Arjun: implement metric name registry and metadata (due 2026-03-15).
- Lena: prototype p95 aggregation in ingestion and demo dashboard (due 2026-03-22).
- Diego: wire the tracing sampling rules into the runtime config endpoint + manual console toggle (due 2026-04-05).
- Maya: run a 2-week experiment with baseline 0.5% sampling on staging to measure cost and tail capture (start 2026-03-07).

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- When sharing with product-hosted-api, emphasize customer_tier tag: dedicated customers need per-tenant dashboards and sampling knobs.
- Keep examples in dashboards anchored to a single route first (simpler UX).
- Link runbooks to each alert panel — don’t leave the dashboard without next-step actions.

References / quick links:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Signal+Catalog+Draft
- Jira epic: JIRA-OBS-47
- PR for sampling library changes: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/256

Last thoughts:
This is intentionally pragmatic — we can iterate once we have baseline telemetry. Focus on naming consistency and trace enrichment first; dashboards and sampling policies can be tuned after 2 weeks of real data.

-- maya
